title: Every item included in a Spell poses a security risk to Sky, so inclusion is never cost-free
content:
Among the considerations for determining Executive Sheet content, A.1.10.2.4.1.1 states plainly: "Every item included in the Spell poses a security risk to Sky."

The usual mental model is that some changes are risky and others are routine, and that routine ones can be added freely. This provision denies that. Even a well-understood internal payment consumes reviewer attention, adds an ordering interaction with other actions, and enlarges the surface where a transcription error can hide.

Treating risk as additive per item changes the default. The question stops being "is there a reason to exclude this?" and becomes "is there a reason to include this *now*?" — because every marginal item costs something even when nothing about it is suspicious.

This premise is what the rest of the process spends provisions cashing out. It is why the Spell Crafter may demand removals from an oversized Spell (A.1.10.2.4.3.1.3), why non-crucial items are dropped when sensitive modules are onboarded, and why removal is made cheap through the Executive Vote queue. Without the premise, all of those look like arbitrary friction; with it, they are direct consequences.
description: A.1.10.2.4.1.1 makes risk additive per item rather than a property of risky items, which is what justifies stripping non-critical content from complex Spells.
